mergeState()

The mergeState() method performs a merge-style state update on a FeatureCell. It enters the Merge stage of the pipeline and combines the current committed state with a supplied incoming value using the active Merge behavior.

Unlike replaceState(), which replaces state entirely, mergeState() computes a structural combination between the existing state and the resolved incoming value before downstream pipeline stages execute.

Method Contract Summary

  • Must be called after initialize()
  • Executes the full pipeline (see Full Pipeline Flow diagram)
  • Uses exactly one active Merge behavior
  • Does not mutate existing state directly
  • Returns a Promise<void> that resolves when pipeline execution completes
Note

The structural outcome of mergeState() is determined entirely by the active Merge behavior. By default, arrays are replaced. If an object merge behavior is configured, objects are merged according to that behavior’s strategy. Exactly one merge behavior must be active per FeatureCell.

Best Practices

Avoid Pre-Computing State in Merge Payloads

A common anti-pattern when using Merge is reading the current State, combining it with new data in consumer code, and passing the pre-computed result to the as the merge payload.

Anti-Pattern
{{`merge(entry: Example): void {
  const current = this.state.value() ?? [];
  this.#vault.mergeState({
    loading: false,
    value: [...current, entry],
    error: null
  });
}
`}}
 
{{`function merge(entry: Example): void {
  const current = exampleCell.state.value ?? [];
  exampleCell.mergeState({
    loading: false,
    value: [...current, entry],
    error: null
  });
}
`}}

This pattern reads State at call time and freezes the Snapshot into the merge payload. When Controllers that govern execution timing are attached to the FeatureCell — such as those that throttle, debounce, or delay Pipeline execution — the State may change between the moment the payload is constructed and the moment the Pipeline processes it. The pre-computed payload then merges against a State that no longer matches the Snapshot it was built from, producing incorrect results.

Instead, pass only the new data as the merge payload and delegate the combination logic to a Merge Behavior. provides purpose-built merge Behaviors through the addons package that handle array accumulation, property merging, and other common strategies. These Behaviors operate inside the Pipeline at the correct execution point, ensuring they always merge against the current resolved State.

Recommended Pattern
{{`merge(entry: Example): void {
  this.#vault.mergeState({
    loading: false,
    value: [entry],
    error: null
  });
}
`}}
 
{{`function merge(entry: Example): void {
  exampleCell.mergeState({
    loading: false,
    value: [entry],
    error: null
  });
}
`}}

Selecting an appropriate merge Behavior from the /addons ensures that State combination occurs deterministically within the Pipeline, regardless of which Controllers are attached.

Method Description
mergeState<T>

inputs:

  • incoming: StateInputType<T>
  • options?: MergeConfig

return:

  • Promise<void>
 Submits a merge-style state update into the pipeline. The incoming value is resolved and structurally combined with the current committed state using the active Merge behavior before downstream stages execute.
Merge Options
Option Description
clearUndefined: boolean When true, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in state clearing. When false (default), undefined preserves the current state and produces no structural change.

Merge options influence only the Merge stage. They do not alter resolve behavior, operators, filters, reducers, or emit-state callbacks.

Accepted State Input Types

The mergeState() method accepts a wide range of input types defined by StateInputType<T>. These inputs determine how the Resolve stage interprets and prepares the incoming value before the Merge stage executes.

Note

All accepted input types are normalized during the Resolve stage before reaching the Merge stage. Regardless of input form, the pipeline ultimately operates on a resolved candidate value that is structurally merged with the current committed state.

Example

The mergeState() method submits a candidate value into the pipeline, where it is resolved, structurally merged with the current state, and then processed through operators, filters, reducers, and taps before state commitment.

What this does

  • Submits an incoming value for merge-style processing
  • Combines it with the current committed state
  • Runs the full downstream pipeline
  • Commits the final snapshot if not suppressed

Example: Merging Default State

{{`
@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {

  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  updateName() {
    this.vault.mergeState([{ name: 'Alice' }]);
  }
}

// If current state is:
// [{ name: 'John', age: 30 }]
//
// After merge (default merge behavior):
// this.vault.state.value()
// [{ name: 'Alice' }]
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: [{ name: 'John', age: 30 }] 
});

employeeCell.initialize();

employeeCell.mergeState([{ age: 31 }]);

// After merge (default merge behavior):
// employeeCell.state.value 
// [{ age: 31 }]
`}}
Note

The structural outcome of mergeState() is determined entirely by the active Merge behavior. By default, arrays are replaced. If an object merge behavior is configured, object combination follows that behavior’s defined strategy. Exactly one merge behavior must be active per FeatureCell.
